free_tier.stated: No free tier, but a free startup credit that needs no card. The Micro card is USD 0.10 a month, billed at 0.000135 an hour: 128 MB RAM, 1 GB NVMe, Economy CPU, IOPS and network tiers, NAT IPv4 with 2 TCP and 2 UDP ports, and an IPv6 /64 per location. A minimum account top-up of USD 3 applies after registration, so USD 0.10 is the run rate and USD 3 is the first payment.

retention.stated: hourly billing, cancel anytime; the about page says 'If you put data on TierHive, we do everything possible to avoid any data loss, but in the event it happens, we will not recover it for you, you get a fresh, blank VPS'; the vendor states services auto-stop when credit runs out and are deleted about 3 days later

egress.terms: no GB allowance at all: 'We do not give any specific arbitrary GB or TB number' - three network tiers plus a fair-use QoS policy, with burst to twice the advertised speed for 10 seconds

interface_detail: KVM guest with root; ports and the external IP are read from the panel's Subnet Config page or from /tmp/ports written by a deployment recipe
tooling: any SSH client; a netinfo endpoint at control.tierhive.com/simple/netinfo returns the port map for a token in /opt/th-simple-token, which makes the mapping scriptable
chaining: the cheapest always-on machine found anywhere in this corpus at USD 0.10 a month, with one UDP port to spare for WireGuard and an IPv6 /64 that has almost the full port range

limits.value: 2 TCP and 2 UDP forwarded ports per VPS, the first TCP port being SSH
no byte allowance; network is tiered and policed by fair use, with the cap stepped down 10 Mbit/s an hour while a guest holds 100 Mbit/s average
a USD 3 minimum top-up after registration, which at USD 0.000135 an hour is about 30 months of Micro runtime; the top-up is the first payment, not the monthly rate

binding_note: two UDP ports is the whole inbound budget, and 128 MB of RAM caps what runs; the network has no byte ceiling to hit first.

identity_cost.detail: email, username and password only: the registration form has six fields, being username, email, password and four policy ticks, with no card, address, phone or ID field. The feature list states 'No credit card required' and the vendor states the free trial credit 'does not require a credit card or validation'. Payment, when the free credit runs out, is through FastSpring as merchant of record, which accepts credit and debit cards and charges the buyer's local VAT rate. No card hold is stated anywhere read. The terms bar free and disposable email addresses and bar signup from China, Russia, Brazil, Vietnam and Iran.

reliability_note: the vendor calls itself 'a no-SLA, budget service' and says 'it is not the place to host things you demand uptime for'; the status page showed every location operational on 2026-10-24 with 99.98 to 100 percent 90-day uptime; the terms bar signup from China, Russia, Brazil, Vietnam and Iran and reserve the right to suspend without warning

notes: The USD 0.10 row survives the checkout check and gets stronger. Registration is six fields with no card, no address, no phone and no ID, so this is the only sub-dollar machine in the band a buyer can actually start without a payment instrument. The first payment is not USD 0.10 but USD 3, a minimum top-up that the vendor says never expires and lasts about 30 months at this rate, so the effective annual cost is USD 1.20 of run rate against USD 3 of float. Two things are better evidenced today than before. The vendor's own recipe library lists 'WireGuard on smallest VPS on TierHive', which is a first-party statement that WireGuard runs on this exact tier, not an inference from a port count. And the status page shows every location operational with 99.98 to 100 percent 90-day uptime, which is the first uptime evidence in the band. The binding constraint is the two UDP ports and the 128 MB, not the price: one WireGuard listener uses half the UDP budget and leaves nothing for a second tunnel. Payment beyond the free credit goes through FastSpring at the buyer's local VAT rate, so a 20 percent VAT country pays USD 0.12 a month rather than USD 0.10. Not established: the card hold at the first top-up, and whether the USD 0.10 tier is deployable at every listed location or only some.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 0.000135 an hour x 730 = USD 0.09855 a month, which the vendor prints as '$0.10/mo'. Ten hours a day is 0.000135 x 300 = USD 0.0405. Hourly billing means a stopped machine costs only storage. The USD 3 minimum top-up / 0.09855 = about 30 months of 24/7 runtime.
